edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds, without setoff, deduction or withholding (except as required by applicable law). The Purchase Price shall not be subject to adjustment.
2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 20 business days after signing, or at such other time as the parties may agree in writing.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that, to the Seller’s knowledge, the financial statements made available to the Buyer have been prepared in all material respects in accordance with the accounting principles used in their preparation and fairly present in all material respects the financial position and results of operations reflected therein, subject to the qualifications and disclosures set forth in the applicable disclosure schedules.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and non-public information received from the other party in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby, and shall not disclose such information except to its affiliates and its and their respective representatives who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations, or as required by law, regulation or court order (in which case, to the extent legally permitted, the disclosing party shall give prior notice and reasonably cooperate with efforts to limit disclosure). This Section does not restrict information that is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price; Closing Adjustment. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 in cash by wire transfer of immediately available funds (the “Closing Payment”), subject to adjustment as set forth in this Section. The Closing Payment shall be adjusted dollar-for-dollar for (a) the Company’s cash, (b) indebtedness, (c) transaction expenses, and (d) working capital above or below an agreed target working capital amount, in each case as of the Closing and determined in accordance with accounting principles and illustrative calculations to be agreed by the parties. The Seller shall deliver a good-faith estimated closing statement before Closing, and the parties shall prepare and review a post-Closing statement under procedures to be set forth in the definitive agreement, including reasonable access to relevant books and records and a period for review and objections. Any disputed items not resolved by the parties shall be submitted to an independent accounting firm for final determination, acting as an expert and not an arbitrator, within the limits of the parties’ submissions. Any resulting payment shall be made promptly after final determination. No amount may be recovered more than once, and no party may set off amounts except for amounts payable under this agreed adjustment process or indemnification provisions as finally agreed in the definitive agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur following completion of the Buyer’s due diligence and satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in the definitive agreement, with a target of 45 business days after signing. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to complete diligence, documentation, and the Closing promptly. The target date is not an unconditional closing deadline, and Closing shall occur at such other time as the parties may agree in writing or as provided in the definitive agreement.

3. Seller Representations and Warranties. Subject to the negotiated disclosure schedules and customary materiality, knowledge, and other agreed qualifications, the Seller shall make customary representations and warranties regarding the Company’s organization and good standing, authority and enforceability, capitalization, financial statements, absence of undisclosed liabilities, compliance with applicable law, material contracts, taxes, employees and employee matters, litigation, and brokers. The financial-statement representation shall cover the financial statements identified in the disclosure schedules and state that they were prepared in all material respects in accordance with the accounting principles used in their preparation and fairly present in all material respects the financial position and results of operations reflected therein, subject to the qualifications and disclosures set forth in the applicable disclosure schedules. The scope, qualifiers, and exceptions to these representations and warranties remain subject to negotiation and inclusion in the definitive agreement and disclosure schedules.

5. Indemnification. The definitive agreement shall provide for customary Seller indemnification for losses arising from breaches of the Seller’s representations, warranties, and covenants, subject to negotiated survival periods, caps, baskets, exclusions, and procedures. As a basis for negotiation, general representations and warranties shall survive for 18 months after Closing, with a 1% of the Purchase Price deductible basket and an aggregate cap of 10% of the Purchase Price; specified fundamental representations and any other agreed categories may be subject to separately negotiated survival periods and caps. No consequential, punitive, special, or exemplary damages, or damages based on a multiple of earnings or other valuation measure, shall be recoverable except to the extent actually awarded to a third party or otherwise expressly agreed. The definitive agreement shall address mitigation, exclusive remedies, and procedures for third-party claims, and shall prevent duplicate recovery. These provisions do not limit the Buyer’s rights under the agreed purchase price adjustment process or indemnification provisions, subject to their terms.

receiver.private_reasoning: The Seller has moved from a $45 million no-adjustment proposal to $42 million with an adjustment framework, broader representations, and an indemnity starting point. The revised economics are directionally favorable, but $42 million remains only a headline figure: cash, debt, transaction expenses, and working capital mechanics could materially change proceeds. Preserve the Buyer’s diligence and closing-condition flexibility and negotiate a lower base price, with precise accounting principles, target working capital, and review procedures. Improve the indemnity framework by seeking a lower deductible or tipping basket, higher cap, longer survival, and robust fundamental, tax, and covenant coverage. No apparent inadvertent disclosure or suspicious document content appears; metadata is ordinary drafting information and there are no comments, tracked changes, or hidden text.
receiver.observed_irregularities: No apparent privileged or confidential material belonging to the Seller or its counsel was inadvertently disclosed. The file has no comments, tracked changes, or hidden text. Metadata identifies Aldous Finch LLP and a drafting associate and shows a 2013 timestamp, which appears to be routine document metadata rather than revealing negotiating information. The agreement numbering skips Section 4, and several material mechanics remain expressly open for negotiation.
receiver.requested_changes: Please provide a revised draft reflecting the following Buyer positions: (1) reduce the base purchase price to USD 38,000,000, subject to the closing adjustment; define cash, indebtedness, and transaction expenses comprehensively, agree accounting principles and sample calculations, and set a working-capital target based on a mutually agreed methodology and representative historical period; provide a detailed statement, access, objection, and expert-determination process, with the expert limited to disputed items and a reasoned written decision. (2) Preserve the Buyer’s ability to complete diligence and satisfaction or waiver of expressly stated closing conditions; the 45-business-day date should remain a non-binding target and not impose an obligation to close before conditions are met. Include customary interim operating covenants and appropriate termination rights. (3) Expand the Seller’s representations to customary comprehensive coverage, including title to shares and assets, intellectual property, privacy/data security, permits, environmental matters, insurance, related-party arrangements, and no brokers, with appropriate disclosure schedules. Remove or tightly constrain general knowledge and materiality qualifiers where appropriate, and include a bring-down condition at Closing. (4) For indemnification, propose a 24-month survival period for general representations, a tipping basket rather than a deductible (or, alternatively, a lower deductible), and a cap of at least 20% of the purchase price; fundamental representations, taxes, and covenants should have separately negotiated longer survival and appropriate caps, with fundamental representations uncapped or subject to a substantially higher cap. Preserve recovery for fraud and intentional misrepresentation, and clarify that purchase-price adjustments are not subject to indemnity caps or baskets and that no exclusive-remedy provision limits claims for fraud or equitable relief. Please add the missing Section 4 or renumber the draft consistently, and provide a complete definitive-form draft with the proposed disclosure schedules and closing conditions.
receiver.message_back: Thank you for the revised draft. The lower headline price and the addition of adjustment mechanics, broader representations, and an indemnity framework are constructive. The Buyer cannot yet evaluate the USD 42 million figure without the detailed adjustment definitions, agreed accounting principles, and working-capital target; our proposed base price is USD 38 million, subject to those mechanics. We have set out the Buyer’s principal revisions above and are ready to discuss them promptly. Please circulate a complete revised draft addressing these points, including the closing conditions and schedules, so we can assess the overall economics and protections together.
